subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled:false` become a hard authorization boundary for skill directories, or remain an eligibility/prompt control with isolation handled by sandbox and tool policy?
rationale: Both choices are plausible but have different security and compatibility meanings, and the repo policy treats security boundaries, config semantics, and fail-closed behavior as maintainer-owned decisions.

options.title: Define a hard disabled-skill boundary
options.body: Make disabled skills unreadable and non-executable through the supported tool surfaces, with tests and docs that name any sandbox or exec limitations.

options.title: Keep eligibility-only semantics
options.body: Document that disabling a skill hides it from discovery/prompting but does not isolate files or scripts, and direct operators to sandbox/tool policy for hard boundaries.

options.title: Add an explicit strict mode
options.body: Preserve current upgrade behavior by default and add a separately named strict security mode for deployments that want disabled skill directories denied.

recommendation.title: Define a hard disabled-skill boundary
recommendation.body: Make disabled skills unreadable and non-executable through the supported tool surfaces, with tests and docs that name any sandbox or exec limitations.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work spans both the skill loader and agent tool policy layers that would need to agree on the boundary.
